title: Upgrade reuse enforcement from local candidate checks to top-down whole-solution-first governance

scope.subject: Project-wide reuse research and implementation gate

research_summary: Upgrade the existing lightweight Node/Git/npm reuse gate rather than replace it with a heavyweight governance platform. Reuse ADR/MADR decision structure, a Technology Radar-style lifecycle registry, and OpenSSF Scorecard-style evaluation dimensions. Search must proceed from full solutions to frameworks/engines to subsystems to components/assets before custom implementation. Architecture/subsystem tasks must carry a coverage matrix, global-value evaluations, and explicit tradeoffs whenever a lower-level choice is selected over a higher-level candidate. Keep Git hooks and npm lifecycle as the enforcement surface. OPA/Conftest and Backstage were evaluated as higher-level policy/catalog products but rejected for runtime/platform overhead relative to this single repository.

sources.finding: Architecture decisions should record context, alternatives, outcome, tradeoffs, consequences and status, and important decisions should remain available in the workload repository.
MADR provides a lightweight structured decision format designed to make assumptions, considered options and outcomes explicit without turning records into large design documents.
Technology Radar uses Adopt, Trial, Assess and Hold states and requires rationale, alternatives and evaluation criteria before broad adoption.
OpenSSF Scorecard treats maintenance, license and dependency/security signals as separate project-health dimensions rather than reducing a candidate to one local feature.
Conftest can machine-test arbitrary structured JSON/YAML using OPA/Rego and is a mature generic option for policy-as-code.
Backstage models Components inside Systems and Domains, demonstrating why a reusable-solution registry needs multiple abstraction levels instead of a flat library list.

search_ladder.conclusion: A full software-catalog platform exists, but operating Backstage just to govern one repository would cost more than the benefit.
OPA/Conftest can enforce structured policies, but adds a separate binary and Rego toolchain; the existing small Node gate can express the project-specific rules directly.
Reuse the strongest lightweight concepts: ADR-style decisions, Radar lifecycle status and multidimensional candidate evaluation.
Keep the already-working Git pre-commit and npm predev/prebuild enforcement surfaces.

coverage_matrix.decision: Keep the Node gate as the enforcement runtime; no additional service or binary.
Encode the search ladder explicitly in the record schema and reject missing upper-level searches.
Use a version-controlled registry JSON rather than deploy a catalog service.

coverage_matrix.capability: global-value comparison instead of single-regression rejection
coverage_matrix.decision: Require multidimensional candidate evaluation and machine-calculate a global value score; selecting against a higher score requires an explicit override.

candidates.name: Backstage Software Catalog as governance platform
candidates.reason: Excellent system/component catalog model, but deploying and maintaining a platform is disproportionate for one repository.

candidates.name: OPA / Conftest policy engine
candidates.reason: Strong generic policy enforcement, but a separate Go binary and Rego language are unnecessary overhead for the small repository-local rule set.

candidates.name: Existing Node reuse gate extended with top-down schema
candidates.license: Project code informed by reusable open methodologies
candidates.reason: Preserves the proven Git/npm enforcement path while adding the missing whole-solution search ladder, registry, coverage matrix and global-value checks.

candidates.name: Technology Radar-style registry status
candidates.reason: Adopt/Trial/Assess/Hold is compact, understandable and prevents rediscovering or accidentally re-adopting rejected/held solutions.

candidates.name: OpenSSF-style multidimensional evaluation
candidates.reason: Reuse the idea of separate maintenance/license/health dimensions; do not make the external CLI a mandatory dependency.

candidates.name: Git hooks plus npm lifecycle enforcement
candidates.reason: Already installed, zero additional service, and proven to block unapproved implementation files.

decision.rationale: Retain the minimal repository-local enforcement runtime, but upgrade its data model using established ADR/catalog/radar/scorecard concepts. This captures the system-level reuse that the old gate missed without introducing a governance platform larger than the project.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: Backstage has broader catalog coverage, but its service/platform footprint and operational cost outweigh that gain for one repository; we reuse its hierarchy concept in a static registry.
OPA/Conftest is a more general policy engine, but the additional binary and Rego maintenance do not improve this repository's four-level search logic enough to justify the integration cost.

decision.fallback: If the Node policy grows beyond a single-repository scope, move the same JSON records to Conftest/OPA or a Backstage catalog without changing the decision schema.
